The '''Players Committee''' (PC) is the volunteer group that took over support of ''Star Wars'' CCG from Decipher in 2002. It created Virtual cards, reorganized them into Virtual Blocks in 2009, and Reset the tournament pool in 2014. For rules by era see [[Rulebooks]]; for constructed pools see [[Formats]]; for Virtual packaging eras see [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]], [[:Category:Virtual Legacy sets|Virtual Blocks]] and [[:Category:Current Virtual sets|Current Virtual]].

== Timeline (high level) ==

=== Decipher era and handoff ===

Decipher published ''Star Wars'' CCG from 1995 through [[Theed Palace]] (2001) and related products. When Decipher announced the license was leaving, it publicly formed a '''Players' Committee''' / Player Advocate structure so fans could continue organized play, rulings, and support.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002; letter dated 25 January 2002)</ref>

[[Warren Holland]] first outlined the committee in a ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' special broadcast on 28 December 2001, the day the end of the license was announced. He described a non-profit, all-volunteer "Players Committee for Star Wars CCGs" of top players and playtesters, which Decipher would support free of charge with email, listserv, web and office facilities. It would be the community's voice on the game's future and oversee rules support and FAQs. At the end of April 2002 Decipher would turn over tournament prize support, the web pages and World Championship duties, and donate reference cards. The committee would also choose existing cards and post replacement game text for them to make them tournament legal, and would become self-governing once its members were selected.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZpXfkPyurfE&t=1332s Radio Free Decipher Special Broadcast (28 December, 2001): Warren Holland and the Players Committee], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 18 February 2022), at 22:12. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZpXfkPyurfE Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Special Broadcast (28 December 2001) transcript]].</ref> By 11 January 2002 just over 200 people had applied; Decipher said the names of applicants not chosen would be passed to the committee.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8aNpe-I-KQk&t=90s Broadcast 110 - Radio Free Decipher (11 January, 2002): SWCCG Player's Committee, ST/LOTR News], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 01:30. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-8aNpe-I-KQk Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 110 transcript]].</ref>

Decipher's Star Wars Announcement page invited players to '''volunteer for the players' committee'''. It listed a volunteer contact alongside Holland/Jones and Lucas Licensing contacts, and linked the 25 January 2002 Players' Committee announcement.<ref name="deciphercall">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020601152726/http://decipher.com/starwars/announcement122801.html The Star Wars Announcement], decipher.com (Wayback, 1 June 2002)</ref> The PC Advocates came from that call for volunteers.

On '''25 January 2002''', Warren Holland (Chairman &amp; CEO) announced the '''first team of Star Wars Player Advocates''' on Decipher's Players' Committee page.<ref name="pc1" /> The letter names Advocate roles for player, tournament, rules and gameplay support. It describes a Norfolk meeting to turn the game over to players and teases a forthcoming virtual-card pool and timetable. Game Players Network would help with communications and prize shipping after 30 April 2002.<ref name="pc1" />

Advocate and Advocate Council rosters are listed on [[Players Committee advocates]]. They run from the first six Advocates and early Council members such as [[Doug Taylor]], [[Josh Radke]] and [[John Arendt]] to the PC organization charts of 2021 and 2024.

On '''29 April 2002''', Game Players Network reported that Decipher would donate over one million dollars in product, promotional materials and financial backing to the Players Committee.<ref name="gpn2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610202816/http://www.gameplayersnetwork.com/card/games.asp?gm=starwars Game Players Network - Star Wars CCG index], Wayback 10 June 2002</ref>

=== Virtual program begins (2002) ===

The PC announced its '''first Virtual Card Set''' on '''12 February 2002''', targeting release on '''4 March 2002''' and Virtual Set #2 on '''6 May 2002'''. Previews ran 25 February-1 March 2002, and the cards were distributed as PDFs on decipher.com.<ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net, 12 February 2002</ref>

Virtual Card Set #1, released on '''5 March 2002''', had twelve Premiere-based (V) slips and became '''tournament-legal on Saturday, 9 March 2002'''.<ref name="decivs1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], decipher.com (Wayback)</ref>

The early printable slips used a modifier/sleeve presentation very different from later Block-era and current Virtual packaging.<ref name="vc1pdf">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050813215254/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/virtual/VirtualCards1.pdf VirtualCards1.pdf], decipher.com (Wayback, 13 August 2005)</ref>

From 2002 to 2009 the PC released '''numbered Virtual Sets''' and [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]].<ref name="swpl">[https://star-wars.pl/Tekst/1963,Star_Wars_CCG_Virtual_Sets.html Star Wars CCG Virtual Sets], star-wars.pl (chronology)</ref> The set index is on [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]].

=== Reorg / "Blocks" (about September 2009) ===

Main articles: [[2009 Virtual Block Reorganization]], [[Virtual Sets to Virtual Blocks]].

In 2009 the PC reorganized the '''previous 18 virtual sets''' into six thematic blocks, with '''Official text as of 7 December 2009'''.<ref name="blockreorg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf VirtualBlock1.pdf]</ref> Block releases continued after the reorganization, such as Block 6.3 Mercenaries on '''15 March 2010'''.<ref name="swpl" />

The official slips library lists '''Legacy Virtual Sets (2002-2009)''' separately from '''Legacy Virtual Blocks (2009-2014)'''.<ref name="slips">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/virtual-slips/ Virtual Slips / Files], starwarsccg.org</ref>

Block pages are [[Virtual Block 1]]-[[Virtual Block 9]] and [[Virtual Shields]]; the era overview is [[Virtual Legacy]]. Blocks were not a lossless rename of VS1-18: presentation, organization, errata and the legal card pool could change. Virtual cards could be '''dropped''' far more easily than physical product could be reprinted.

=== Advanced Rulebook 2.0 (Legacy Virtual rules) ===

During the Legacy Virtual period the PC published [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0]]. Among other revisions it introduced the [[Mission]] card type. That book is '''not''' the current tournament Advanced Rulebook.

=== 2014 Virtual Card Reset ===

In '''Fall 2014''' the PC Reset the competitive virtual pool; [[Virtual Set 0]] and [[Virtual Set D]] are dated '''24 September 2014'''. The Alternate Format Tournament Guide separates '''Standard''' (post-Reset virtual icons) from '''Legacy''' (the pre-Reset black-diamond / Block pool). It names the 2014 World Championships as the last championship circuit on the old pool.<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), via [[Formats]]</ref>

Current Virtual sets have continued since the Reset ([[:Category:Current Virtual sets]]). The current tournament rules are the [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]] (2023 edition).

=== Current site ===

An early official Players Committee website was '''swccgpc.com''', which carried news by October 2002.<ref name="swccgpc2002">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106101746/http://www.swccgpc.com/ The SWCCG Player's Committee], swccgpc.com (Wayback, 6 November 2002)</ref>

On '''10 June 2009''', the PC moved to a new server and began forwarding to its new domain, '''StarWarsCCG.org'''.<ref name="domain2009">[https://web.archive.org/web/20090706102740/http://www.starwarsccg.org/news/news.php?id=69 New Domain and Server], starwarsccg.org news.php?id=69 (posted 10 June 2009; Wayback capture 6 July 2009)</ref>

Organized play, slips, formats and news remain at [https://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org].

'''Errata and drops:''' Virtual text is easier to revise or remove from legality than a physical print run. A card's (V) text in 2002, its Block-era presentation and any current Virtual descendant may differ, so the current cardlist does not always show the historical text.
